extracted.intended_audience: IP office statisticians, policymakers, researchers, and intellectual property professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction and interpretation of WIPO statistical metrics and procedural indicators for trademarks and industrial designs (counts, equivalents, office procedural metrics, time-to-decision, and normalized intensity measures). Useful for cross‑office comparison and trend analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration class count by office
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of trademark registration classes processed by each office, broken down into resident and non-resident components and presented by office (and origin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables show 'Total', 'Resident', 'Non-resident', and sometimes 'Total (a)'. Footnotes indicate that data by origin may be incomplete because some offices do not report detailed origin information; Madrid-designation-only offices may cause incompleteness. 'n.a.' = not applicable; '..' = not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent registration class count
rubrics_metrics.description: An adjusted registration class count that accounts for regional offices by converting registrations at regional offices into the equivalent number of registrations across their member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to harmonize data from regional offices (e.g., OAPI, BOIP, EUIPO). Footnotes explain how equivalence is calculated and exceptions (e.g., ARIPO and EAPO treatment differs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrations in force (by office) and year-over-year change
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of trademark registrations active/in force at each office and the change in that number compared to the previous year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported alongside 'Change over previous year' (positive/negative). Useful for measuring growth or decline in active registrations across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data completeness and caveats for registration counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes and caveats about missing/incomplete data (e.g., Madrid-only data, offices not reporting origin breakdowns) and meaning of special codes ('n.a.', '..').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes (a)–(i) detail specific reasons for incompleteness (Madrid-only, no national office, aggregated direct registration counts, etc.). Users are warned that some registration class counts by origin are incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total applications processed (procedural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of trademark applications an office processed in the reporting year (may include several processing outcomes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the denominator for outcome shares. WIPO warns totals may be incomplete due to omission of elements by an office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications registered (procedural outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number (and share) of processed applications that resulted in registration at the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare grant rates across offices; differences in examination regimes must be accounted for when comparing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total rejections (procedural outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number (and share) of processed applications formally rejected by the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some offices show particularly high rejection shares; cross-office procedural differences can drive these differences, so caution is advised in interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawn or abandoned applications (procedural outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number (and share) of processed applications that were withdrawn by applicants or abandoned during prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High withdrawal/abandonment shares may reflect applicant behaviour, office practice, or procedural stages; examples: Mexico, Thailand, Bangladesh had large shares withdrawn/abandoned in industrial designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications pending
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of trademark applications pending at the end of the reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates backlog; needs to be interpreted with other throughput/time metrics and local procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of examiners (FTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Full-time equivalent count of examiners at the office handling trademark or design examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTE definition provided; used to normalize productivity and capacity measures. WIPO cautions that procedural differences limit direct comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: First office action (days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average number of days from filing to the first office action issued by the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported per office as a timing metric for examination responsiveness. Interpret with care because counting rules and what constitutes 'first action' can vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final office decision (days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average number of days from filing (or other start point) to the final decision on an application at the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess total time-to-resolution; cross-office procedural heterogeneity (e.g., substantive examination vs registration by default) affects comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designs in industrial design applications (application design count)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of individual designs contained in industrial design applications, i.e., counting multiple designs allowed within a single application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application design counts harmonize offices that permit multiple designs per application with those that allow only one; reported as 'designs contained in applications' and differ from application counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent design count (for industrial designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: An adjusted design count that multiplies each design filed at a regional office by the number of member states to obtain an equivalent count across member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit method: OAPI (17), BOIP (3), EUIPO (27) multiply by member counts; ARIPO and EAPO do not register designs with automatic region-wide applicability and are treated differently (counted as one application abroad or resident+abroad depending on applicant residence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident versus non-resident classification (origin vs office data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between office data (applications received by an office) and origin data (applications filed by applicants at their home or foreign offices). 'Origin' is defined as the country/territory of the stated residence of the holder of an international registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resident = filed at home office; Non-resident = filed abroad. Footnotes clarify how some aggregated direct registration counts cannot be split into resident and non-resident components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident design count per USD 100 billion GDP
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalized metric: number of resident application design counts adjusted per USD 100 billion of GDP for an origin, to compare filing intensity relative to economic size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare filing intensity across origins; examples and rankings (China, Rep. of Korea, Türkiye) are given. Changes over a decade are reported for interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident design count per million population
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalized metric: number of resident design counts per million population for an origin, to compare filing intensity relative to population size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for cross-origin intensity comparisons (Rep. of Korea, Türkiye, Italy, Germany noted). Useful alongside GDP-normalized metric to understand per-capita activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping Locarno classes into 12 industry sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregation of the 32 Locarno classes into 12 industry sectors to highlight predominant industry sectors for design filings (e.g., furniture and household goods, textiles and accessories, tools and machines, electricity and lighting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows sectoral analysis and identification of top sectors by office/origin. The top three sectors often account for large shares of filings at offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active registrations and typical term
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of active/ in-force industrial design registrations at offices and the typical maximum duration of industrial design rights (generally up to 15 years from filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as global totals and by office; growth rates year-over-year are highlighted. 'Active registrations' used to measure the stock of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average age of active industrial design registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Average number of years since first registration among the active industrial design registrations held at an office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives insight into the turnover and longevity of registered designs (examples: Israel 10.1 years, China 2.9 years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination outcome distribution for industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of processed industrial design applications that are registered, rejected, or withdrawn/abandoned at each office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported shares allow comparisons; examples include EUIPO (97.7% registered), UK (94.9%), China (91.2%), and offices with high rejection shares such as Israel (35.1%), Saudi Arabia (26.4%), Viet Nam (24.2%), US (22%). Differences in procedures affect comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic/regional distribution of filings (by region and office)
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of application/design counts by region (Asia, Europe, North America, LAC, Africa, Oceania) and concentration of activity among top offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to show regional shares and trends (Asia 69.3% in 2021). Also highlights concentration (top 20 offices account for ~93–95% of activity) and growth/decline by region/office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trends and historical series (time series of applications and designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Longitudinal series of application and design counts (e.g., 2007–2021, 1883–2021) to identify trends, growth rates, and structural changes across decades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures and commentary explain historical growth patterns (e.g., China’s rapid growth since 1985) and year-to-year rate changes; used for trend analysis and contextual interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparability caveat for procedural and outcome metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit caution that differences in office procedures, definitions, and reporting practices make full harmonization difficult and advise caution when making cross-office comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WIPO note: 'Every effort has been made to compile procedural data based on common definitions and concepts, but procedural differences make it extremely difficult to fully harmonize such data.' Users should interpret comparative metrics (times, outcomes, examiner counts) with caution.
